problem: End-to-end DRL image-goal navigation methods mostly improve fusion of the current observation and the goal image, and fail to fully exploit the temporal relationships in the agent's visual-action history. Modular methods rely on explicit map construction, which struggles in complex, unstructured environments.
motivation: Image-goal navigation needs spatio-temporal reasoning over past observations and actions. The paper proposes that self-supervised masked prediction over visual-action embeddings can supply this temporal signal to the policy.
key_idea: A dual-attention transformer shared between masked visual-action embedding prediction (self-supervised) and RL policy generation, so the policy benefits from spatio-temporal representation learning over the agent's history (DaMVA).
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that jointly using the masked-prediction objective and a shared dual-attention transformer for the policy improves performance and generalization over 12 baselines on Gibson, MP3D and HM3D.
method: Masked visual-action modeling: a self-supervised transformer predicts masked portions of the agent's history of visual and action embeddings.
Dual-attention shared transformer: one transformer handles both masked representation learning and policy generation, promoting spatio-temporal reasoning.
DRL policy: an end-to-end reinforcement learning policy outputs actions directly from visual input plus the goal image.
